title: Player's Game Card
description: Nine-page player-created table reference covering turn actions, conditions, movement and exploration, character advancement, rites, equipment, transformation, doors, and chases. Player-facing entries are concise transcriptions; DM-only Insane and Lost mechanics remain hidden.

paragraphs: Take the Attack action using the weapon, unarmed strike, or feature available to your hunter.
Perform a Rite or Whisper using its listed performing time, range, duration, and effect.
Use the optional climbing-on-a-bigger-creature rules when the DM allows it.
Move up to twice your current movement.
Make an opposed Strength or Dexterity check. The opponent has disadvantage if it is holding the object with both hands.
Your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks until your next turn.
Attacks against you have disadvantage, and you make Dexterity rolls with advantage. The benefit ends if you are incapacitated or your speed drops to 0.
Give another creature advantage on an attack or ability check.
Devote your attention to finding something. Depending on the search, the DM may call for Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation).
Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check against the opposing Wisdom (Perception) check.
Make a Strength versus Strength check to move through an opponent's space.
Make a Dexterity versus Dexterity check to move through an opponent's space.
Choose a trigger and the reaction you will take in response, or ready a Rite and hold its release.
Contest Strength against Strength or Dexterity to push an opponent 5 feet back, to the side, or prone.
You can interact with one object for free during your turn, such as drawing a weapon or opening a door. Use this action to interact with a second object.
Make Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) contested by the grappler's Strength (Athletics). Other restraints may require a check chosen by the DM.
You can take a bonus action only when a feature, Rite, or other rule explicitly says you can do something as a bonus action.

After attacking with a light melee weapon, make one attack with a different light melee weapon held in the other hand. Do not add your ability modifier to the damage unless it is negative. A thrown weapon may be thrown instead.
A reaction is an instant response to a trigger and can occur on your turn or someone else's turn.
When an enemy leaves your reach, use your reaction to make one melee attack before it moves away. Teleportation and forced movement do not provoke this attack.
When the trigger you specified occurs, use your reaction to execute the action prepared with Ready.
You cannot see and automatically fail checks that require sight. Attacks against you have advantage; your attacks have disadvantage.
You cannot attack the charmer or target it with harmful abilities or effects. The charmer has advantage on checks to interact socially with you.
You cannot hear and automatically fail checks that require hearing.

Exhaustion has six cumulative levels: disadvantage on ability checks; speed halved; disadvantage on attacks and saves; hit point maximum halved; speed 0; death. A long rest reduces exhaustion by one level.
You have disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is in sight, and cannot willingly move closer to it.
Your speed becomes 0 and cannot benefit from bonuses. The condition ends if the grappler is incapacitated or you are moved outside its reach.
You cannot take actions or reactions.

You cannot be seen without magic or a special sense and are heavily obscured for hiding. Your location can still be revealed by sound or tracks. Attacks against you have disadvantage; your attacks have advantage.
You are incapacitated and cannot move or speak. You fail Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks against you have advantage, and a hit from within 5 feet is critical.

You and nonmagical carried objects become solid inanimate substance. You are incapacitated, unaware, ten times heavier, and stop aging. You fail Strength and Dexterity saves, resist all damage, and are immune to poison and disease.
You have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
You can only crawl until you stand. Your attacks have disadvantage. Attacks from within 5 feet have advantage against you; attacks from farther away have disadvantage.
Your speed becomes 0. Attacks against you have advantage, your attacks have disadvantage, and you have disadvantage on Dexterity saves.
You are incapacitated, cannot move, and can speak only falteringly. You fail Strength and Dexterity saves, and attacks against you have advantage.
You are incapacitated, cannot move or speak, are unaware, drop held objects, and fall prone. You fail Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks have advantage, and a hit from within 5 feet is critical.
You gain the Insane condition when current Madness equals or exceeds Max Sanity. It ends when Madness is reduced below Max Sanity. Your DM resolves the condition's hidden effects.

Each 5 feet moved costs 5 feet of speed. You may switch between movement speeds, subtracting distance already moved. Other creatures' spaces are difficult terrain, and you cannot willingly end movement in another creature's space.
Each 5 feet climbed costs 10 feet of movement. A difficult climb may require Strength (Athletics).
Each 5 feet swum costs 10 feet of movement. Difficult water may require Strength (Athletics).
Dropping prone costs no movement. While prone you must crawl or use magic to move.
Each 5 feet crawled costs 10 feet of movement.
Standing costs half your speed. You cannot stand without enough movement remaining or when your speed is 0.
With a 10-foot run-up, leap 3 + Strength modifier feet. A standing jump covers half that distance. The DM may allow Strength (Athletics) to jump higher.

With a 10-foot run-up, leap up to your Strength score in feet. A standing jump covers half. Obstacles may require DC 10 Strength (Athletics), and landing in difficult terrain may require DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics).
Moving through difficult terrain costs an additional 5 feet for every 5 feet moved.
You may drag or carry a grappled creature. Your speed is halved unless it is at least two sizes smaller than you.
Vision depends on obscurity and illumination. A heavily obscured area effectively blinds a creature trying to see through it.

paragraphs: Some creatures perceive their environment through extraordinary senses.

rows: Perceive surroundings within range without relying on sight
Within range, darkness appears as dim light and dim light as bright light; color is not discerned
See through normal and magical darkness, perceive invisible creatures, detect visual illusions and transformations, and see into other planes within range

paragraphs: Hold breath for 10 × (1 + Constitution modifier) rounds, minimum 5. After breath runs out, survive for Constitution modifier rounds; at the start of the next turn, drop to 0 HP and begin dying.
A target with total cover cannot be targeted directly, but may still be affected by area effects.
For bigger doors, double or triple the Hit Points and increase the force-open DC by 5.
During a chase, a participant can Dash 3 + Constitution modifier times. Each additional Dash requires a DC 10 Constitution check at the end of the turn or causes one Exhaustion level.

At the end of each round, each quarry makes Dexterity (Stealth), compared with pursuers' passive Perception. If the quarry is never out of sight, the check fails. A higher result lets the quarry escape; otherwise the chase continues.

tables.caption: Escape factors
rows: Lead pursuer is a ranger or proficient in Survival

paragraphs: At the end of a participant's turn, roll d20 on the appropriate table. On 11–20 there is no complication. A participant may spend inspiration to negate a complication.

Rough brush; DC 10 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics), otherwise 5 feet of difficult terrain

Slippery ground; DC 10 Dexterity save or fall prone
DC 10 Constitution save or be blinded and slowed until end of next turn

Sudden drop; DC 10 Dexterity save or fall 1d4 × 5 feet, taking damage and landing prone

Eldritch Knowledge; Old World History; Investigation; Blood Nature; Religion
Animal Handling; Insight; Medicine; Perception; Survival

paragraphs: Passive Perception = 10 + all Wisdom (Perception) modifiers.
Blood Tinge is gained when leveling. Spend it to add 1d6 to one of your own attack, save, or ability-check d20 rolls; turn a Death Save failure into a success; or reroll any roll.
Rite attack bonus = ability modifier + proficiency bonus. Performing within 5 feet of an enemy imposes disadvantage. Rite save DC = 8 + ability modifier + proficiency bonus + situational modifiers.
Protection, Summoning, Detection, Mind Influence, Evocation, Illusion, and Teleportation.

Concentration ends when you perform another Rite requiring concentration; become incapacitated or die; or fail a check caused by damage, startling phenomena, or vigorous movement. Taking damage calls for Constitution DC 8 + damage taken, separately for each source. Startling phenomena and vigorous movement normally call for DC 10 Constitution.

rows: Pure force of an eldritch being
Burned by coals; falling bookcase; poison needle
Struck by lightning; stumbling into a fire pit
Falling rubble; collapsing tunnel; vat of acid
Compacting walls; whirling blades; lava stream
Submerged in lava; crashing flying fortress
Elemental Fire vortex; jaws of a god-like monster
Rocks fall, everyone dies; campaign ends

paragraphs: The GM may rule that certain weapons or damage types cannot harm an object at all.
Weapon damage, properties, mastery, weight, and carrying category from the Player's Game Card.
Coins, Weapons, Armor, Tools, Hunting Gear, Storage Items, and Unique Items.

rows: Speed reduced by 20 ft; disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks, attacks, and saves

paragraphs: Transformation Level ranges from 0–10. When you gain a level, increase it by 1, then physically roll on the Transformation Table using the new level.
A table result is not always a Transformation. Nothing Happens is not one. Blood Lust is a compulsion. Lost is catastrophic and counts as a Transformation; tell the DM.

Short Rest: reduce the level by 1 and lose all active Transformations; a DC 13 Constitution (Grit) success reduces it by 1 more. Long Rest: reduce to 0 and lose all. The first Unconscious condition after gaining a Transformation reduces the level by 2 and removes all active Transformations, once until another rest or Transformation.
Drink another Blood Vial or suffer 3 Madness. This compulsion is not a Transformation.
Suffer 2 Madness. Add 1d12 to your damage roll and 5 feet to your range for melee damage; suffer 1 Madness when you do.
As a melee attack, bite a creature within 5 feet. On a hit deal 4d3 piercing damage and heal the same amount; suffer 1 Madness.
As an action, gain Blindsight for 10 rounds; suffer 1 Madness.
Your Wisdom (Perception) modifier increases by 5. You may suffer 1 Madness to make a Wisdom (Perception) check with advantage.
Increase Transformation Level first, then roll 1d20 physically and read the column for the new level. The app does not roll for you.
